plan: Second-price auction with independent private values. Dominant strategy: bid your true value. Overbidding risks winning at a price above value; underbidding risks losing when winning would be profitable. With value = 39 and no history to exploit (single round), bid 39 to maximize expected profit. Ties resolve randomly; no benefit to shading given uniform draws and unknown opponents.

[ This is a second-price (Vickrey) auction with independent private values uniformly drawn each round. In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: it maximizes expected profit regardless of others’ strategies. Overbidding risks negative payoff if a higher rival bid sets a price above my value; underbidding risks losing when I would have earned positive surplus. With value 34 and no useful history (single round), I bid exactly 34 to win whenever the second-highest bid is below 34 and pay that second-highest bid. Ties are random; exact truth-telling remains optimal. ]

[ In a sealed-bid second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy. It guarantees winning exactly when the second-highest bid is below your value and paying that second-highest bid, maximizing expected profit. Overbidding risks paying above your value if others bid high; underbidding risks losing profitable wins. With value = 45 (uniform draws 0–49), the best long-run and round-specific strategy is to bid 45. No history to exploit in a single round; focus on truth-telling to maximize expected surplus. ]
